name: Virupaksha Temple
description: Ancient 7th-century Dravidian temple complex dedicated to Lord Shiva with an active bazaar and river bathing ghats.

name: Vijaya Vittala & Stone Chariot
description: Vijayanagara architectural masterpiece with 56 resonant musical pillars and the celebrated monolithic Stone Chariot.

name: Lotus Mahal & Zenana Enclosure
description: Symmetrical lotus-shaped two-storey palace combining Indo-Islamic arches and stone eaves within walled queens’ quarter.

name: Royal Elephant Stables
description: Grand eleven interconnected domed chambers built with distinct Islamic and Hindu vaulted brickwork.

name: Hemakuta Hill Temples
description: Granite boulder hilltop dotted with over thirty pre-Vijayanagara triple-celled sanctuaries overlooking the Tungabhadra valley.

name: Kamalapur Archaeological Museum
description: Four air-cooled galleries preserving Vijayanagara stone statuary, palm-leaf manuscripts, ancient coinage and miniature terrain models.

name: Mango Tree Heritage Dining
description: Sheltered garden khanavali serving North Karnataka Jolada rotti meals, ennegayi curry, and fresh fruit smoothies.

name: KSTDC Hotel Mayura Bhuvaneshwari
description: Karnataka State Tourism Corporation official heritage resort with garden cottages, safe parking, and verified travel desk.

name: Sanapur Lake & Boulders
description: Scenic reservoir on the Anegundi side flanked by granite boulders, quiet trails, and tranquil water reflection.

name: Krishna Temple Complex
description: Erected by Krishnadevaraya in 1513 CE commemorating his victory in Udayagiri, featuring carved Yali columns and stepwell.

name: Amba Vilas Mysore Palace
description: Indo-Saracenic royal seat of the Wadiyar dynasty renowned for stained glass ceilings, carved mahogany, and evening illuminations.

name: Chamundeshwari Temple & Chamundi Hill
description: Historic hill shrine perched 1000 metres above Mysuru with panoramic viewpoints and the giant monolithic Nandi statue.

name: Devaraja Heritage Bazaar
description: Century-old heritage marketplace overflowing with fresh jasmine strands, Mysore betel leaves, aromatic oils, and jaggery piles.

name: Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens
description: Established in 1892, one of India's oldest and most respected zoological parks with extensive botanical gardens and lake walks.

name: St. Philomena's Cathedral
description: Neo-Gothic church with 175-foot twin spires modelled after Germany's Cologne Cathedral and serene catacombs.

name: Abbey Falls
description: Roaring waterfall cascading through lush private coffee and spice plantations, viewed from a hanging pedestrian bridge.

name: Raja's Seat & Musical Gardens
description: Seasonal garden pavilion where Kodagu kings enjoyed sweeping sunset vistas over mist-clad valleys and green hills.

name: Namdroling Monastery (Golden Temple)
description: Prominent Tibetan settlement featuring 40-foot gold-plated Buddha statues, vivid murals, and echoing chanting ceremonies.

name: Dubare Elephant Camp
description: Riverside camp on the banks of river Kaveri where trained naturalists guide elephant bathing and rehabilitation observations.

name: Talakaveri & Brahmagiri Peak
description: Sacred birthplace of river Kaveri nestled high in Brahmagiri hills with stairs ascending to panoramic viewpoint ridges.

name: Mahabaleshwar Temple & Atmalinga
description: Classical 4th-century Dravidian coastal shrine enshrining the sacred Atmalinga with holy dip traditions at Kotiteertha.

name: Om Beach & Coastal Cliff Trail
description: Iconic naturally formed Om-shaped beach flanked by rocky promontories, tide pools, and cliff walks to Half Moon beach.

name: Kudle Beach
description: Broad crescent of soft golden sand fringed by coconut palms and calm surf, accessible by hillside stone pathways.

name: Mirjan Fort
description: 16th-century laterite fortress built by Queen Chennabhairadevi (the Pepper Queen) with bastions, moats, and secret wells.

name: Mullayanagiri Peak
description: The highest peak in Karnataka (1,930 m) featuring misty windswept trails, sage shrine, and breathtaking Western Ghats horizons.

name: Baba Budangiri & Manikyadhara
description: Sacred mountain range associated with Sufi saint Baba Budan who introduced coffee seeds to India, with holy springs.

name: Coffee Yatra Museum
description: Interactive museum curated by the Coffee Board of India displaying coffee processing history, roasting labs, and tasting exhibits.

name: Hebbe Falls
description: Twin cascades falling 168 metres through dense Kemmangundi coffee forests, reached by forest jeep safari trails.

name: Sri Krishna Matha & Kanakana Kindi
description: 13th-century monastery established by saint Madhvacharya where the deity is worshipped through a nine-holed silver window (Kanakana Kindi).

name: St. Mary's Volcanic Basalt Islands
description: Geological monument of columnar hexagonal basalt rock formations created by sub-aerial sub-volcanic activity 88 million years ago.

name: Malpe Beach & Sea Walk
description: Vibrant fishing port beach featuring a dedicated sea walkway projecting into the Arabian Sea with boat jetty access.

name: Kaup Lighthouse & Beach
description: Black-and-white striped 1901 maritime lighthouse built upon giant coastal granite rocks offering stellar sea panoramas.

name: Badami Cave Temples (1 to 4)
description: Four cliffside rock-cut temples excavated between 540 and 578 CE dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Jain Tirthankaras.

name: Agastya Lake & Ghats
description: Sacred water reservoir flanked by towering red sandstone ravines, ancient stone steps, and women washing colorful cotton sarees.

name: Bhuthanatha Temple Complex
description: Poetic 7th-century sandstone temple extending directly into the waters of Agastya lake, creating magical golden reflections.

name: North Fort & Archaeological Museum
description: Challenging climb between red sandstone chasms to upper granaries, Tipu's cannons, and ASI ground gallery of Chalukya sculpture.

name: Virupaksha Temple Pattadakal
description: Erected by Queen Lokamahadevi in 740 CE to commemorate victory over Pallavas; the benchmark for Kailasa temple at Ellora.

name: Mallikarjuna Temple Complex
description: Built simultaneously by Queen Trailokyamahadevi featuring ornate circular pillars carved with scenes from Mahabharata and Panchatantra.

name: Sangameshwara Temple
description: Commissioned by Chalukya King Vijayaditya (696–733 CE), the oldest temple in the main Pattadakal UNESCO quadrangle.

name: Papanatha Temple (Nagara Style)
description: Fascinating northern Nagara-shikhara temple exhibiting experimental fusion of North and South Indian stone carving traditions.

name: Durga Temple (Apsidal Shikhara)
description: Celebrated apsidal (Buddhist Chaitya-shaped) sanctuary with ambulatory colonnade, exquisitely sculpted bracket figures, and sun god reliefs.

name: Lad Khan Temple
description: Experimental hall-style 5th-century stone temple built mimicking traditional timber village assembly halls.

name: Ravanaphadi Rock-Cut Cave
description: 6th-century rock sanctuary hollowed into a sandstone knoll with dramatic dynamic relief of Nataraja flanked by Saptamatrikas.

name: Meguti Jain Temple & Inscription
description: Hilltop stone sanctuary dated precisely to 634 CE containing poet Ravikirti's stone inscription recording the feats of Pulakeshin II.

name: Manjarabad Star Fort
description: Unique eight-pointed octagonal star fort constructed by Tipu Sultan in 1792 with French engineers, offering 360-degree hill views.

name: Bisle Ghat Viewpoint
description: Observation platform overlooking three mountain ranges: Kumara Parvatha, Pushpagiri, and Dodda Betta, immersed in mist.

name: Sakleshwara Swamy Temple
description: Ancient 11th-century Hoysala temple situated on the banks of river Hemavathi from which the town gets its historic name.

name: Magajahalli (Hanbal) Waterfalls
description: Lush 20-foot natural waterfall tucked inside quiet coffee plantations, ideal for gentle foot soaks in crystal waters.

name: Kudremukh Peak Trek
description: 22 km round-trip guided rainforest trek through misty shola woods to the distinctive horse-face ridge summit (1,894 m).

name: Hanuman Gundi Falls
description: Forest-maintained cascade tumbling over 100 feet into a tranquil natural rock bowl, accessed via well-paved 300 steps.

name: Kalaseshwara Temple (Kalasa)
description: Ancient Shiva temple located in the agrahara town of Kalasa on the Bhadra river bank, surrounded by lush arecanut farms.

name: Lakya Dam Reservoir
description: Expansive reservoir framed by deep emerald hills and silent forests, perfect for afternoon photography and birdwatching.

name: Giant Shiva Statue & Kanduka Giri
description: 123-foot colossal Lord Shiva statue overlooking the Arabian Sea, featuring an underground museum narrating the Atmalinga legend.

name: 20-Storey Raja Gopura & Lift Viewpoint
description: 237-foot modern gateway tower with high-speed elevator ascending to the 18th floor for aerial coastal views of the peninsula.

name: Murudeshwar Beach & Promenade
description: Gentle sandy shoreline popular for sunset strolling, fresh tender coconuts, and motorboat rides towards the headland.

name: Netrani Island Scuba & Snorkel Jetty
description: Heart-shaped coral reef island located 19 km offshore, celebrated as Karnataka's primary scuba diving and marine biodiversity sanctuary.

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
description: 9th-century Western Ganga and Hoysala river-island sanctuary worshipping Lord Ranganatha reclining on the coils of serpent Adisesha.

name: Daria Daulat Bagh (Tipu Summer Palace)
description: Intricate teakwood summer palace surrounded by manicured Mughal charbagh gardens, adorned with vibrant 18th-century battle frescoes.

name: Gumbaz Mausoleum
description: Imposing dome mausoleum holding the graves of Tipu Sultan, Hyder Ali, and Fakr-Un-Nisa, fronted by polished black basalt pillars.

name: Sangama (Kaveri & Lokapavani Confluence)
description: Picturesque spot where the branches of river Kaveri and Lokapavani merge, offering traditional coracle boat rides.

name: Bangalore Palace
description: Tudor-style royal estate inspired by Windsor Castle featuring fortified towers, stained glass, and historic royal portrait galleries.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Glasshouse
description: 240-acre botanical haven founded by Hyder Ali in 1760 with 3000-million-year-old Peninsular Gneiss rock and Crystal Palace-styled Glasshouse.

name: Cubbon Park & Vidhana Soudha
description: Green pulmonary core of the city leading to the monumental Neo-Dravidian granite facade of Karnataka's legislative assembly.

name: Tipu Sultan's Fort & Summer Palace
kannadaName: ಟಿಪ್ಪು ಸುಲ್ತಾನ್ ಕೋಟೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬೇಸಿಗೆ ಅರಮನೆ
description: 1791 ornate wooden palace constructed entirely from French-influenced teakwood pillars, arches, and floral wall brackets in the old pete.

name: Jog Falls (Raja, Roarer, Rocket & Rani)
description: Sharavathi river plunging unbroken 253 metres (830 ft) in four distinct cascades down a precipitous chasm in the Western Ghats.

name: Sakrebyle Elephant Camp
description: Renowned forest department elephant camp on the backwaters of Gajanur dam where mahouts bathe wild tuskers each morning.

name: Keladi Rameshwara Heritage Temple
description: 16th-century capital temple of the Keladi Nayakas blending Hoysala, Dravidian, and Vijayanagara styles with ceiling relief of Gandaberunda.

name: Tyavarekoppa Lion & Tiger Safari
description: 250-hectare open sanctuary hosting safari van tours through natural Sahyadri scrub forest habitats.
